title: transient-working-set-leak-hypotheses
content:
TL;DR:
We saw sporadic OOMs on dedicated hosts running long-lived KV-cache workloads. Heap size (reported by driver) was below physical GPU RAM, but allocations failed after ~36–48h of steady traffic. Hypothesis: a pattern of transient allocations plus pinned-host buffers and delayed cudaFree paths (cudaMallocAsync arena fragmentation + stream-synchronization) is slowly stealing usable contiguous device memory. This doc captures reproducer, traces, perf counters, experiments, and short-term mitigations.

Symptoms observed:
- OOMs appear after long uptime (tens of thousands of requests), usually during medium-sized requests (seq_len ~1024, batch 2–4).
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used reports < 95% when OOM happens; but cudaMalloc returns OOM.
- Host-side resident set and swap usage low. No kernel OOMs.
- Heap dumps (allocator stats) show many small free chunks spread across arenas; total free bytes > allocation size but fragmentation prevents large contiguous allocation.
- Reproduces more reliably when KV cache is enabled and client traffic shows high prefix variance.

Reproducer (local):
- Workload: mix of short (len 64) and long (len 1024) requests; 60% short, 40% long; concurrency 12; frequent model swaps (model reload every ~8k reqs) to simulate live rollouts.
- Script (pseudo):
  for i in range(100000):
    choose seq_len from distribution;
    send_request(seq_len, use_kvcache=rand_bool(0.7));
    sleep(0.02)
- Run on dev-GPU (A10x) with CUDA 11.8 and cudamallocasync-enabled allocator.

Key observations & traces:
- cuda-memcheck shows no invalid accesses.
- nvprof/Nsight traces show bursts of short device allocations prior to long-request allocations failing.
- Exported allocator stats (custom hooks) show: many allocations 4–64KB that are short-lived; larger workspace allocations (several hundred MB) are frequent for long requests.
- Heap histogram snapshot before OOM: free segments: many small (4K–64K) fragmented across >1000 regions; largest free block ~120MB while requested workspace needed ~180MB.
- cudaMallocAsync arena logs indicate deferred frees pending on streams; deferred freelist size grows over time until fragmentation prevents coalescing into large block.
- Enabling eager stream synchronization temporarily reduces deferred list but increases tail latency.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Deferred-free semantics of cudaMallocAsync + multi-stream usage prevents coalescing of adjacent freed blocks, causing gradual fragmentation of arena. Short allocations on many streams leave many small stubs that cannot merge until stream completes and queues drained.
2) KV-cache growth leads to frequent pinned host allocations (cudaHostAlloc) and implicit page-locked buffers that interact with device allocator and increase working set pressure; combined with (1) this reduces available contiguous device allocations.
3) Mixed-size allocation patterns (many small ephemeral + occasional large workspace) inherently stress slab or bin-based pools, exposing allocator edge cases where large free extents are split and never rejoined.
4) CUDA driver bug that fails to return certain freed blocks to global free list under heavy concurrency (less likely but possible given vendor driver changes).

Experiments run and results:
- Swap cudaMallocAsync for cudaMalloc (synchronous) in a controlled build: OOMs disappear on same run-length but average latency increased ~8–15%. Interpretation: deferred-free behavior from async allocator is a strong suspect.
- Force stream synchronization (cudaStreamSynchronize) after large-request path: fragmentation growth rate reduced by ~70% and OOMs delayed, but throughput drops.
- Disable KV cache (or cap at small size): failure rate reduced; suggests KV cache contributes to working set pressure.
- Use smaller workspace allocation strategy (split large workspace into multiple smaller allocations with temporary pooling): reduced allocation failures at cost of more allocations; fragmentation rate similar but large contiguous needs avoided.
- Captured cuMemGetInfo over time: free memory oscillates with many small dips; when fragmentation increases, largest contiguous free chunk metric drops sharply (< needed workspace).

Profiler excerpts (sanitized):
- timeline: multiple streams 0x3/0x4/0x6 allocating 8–64KB frequently, freeing; large allocs on stream 0x1 failing.
- allocator log: "deferred_free_count = 18432, pending_bytes = 1.2GB" before failure.

Short-term mitigations (low risk, deployable):
- Add periodic background full-stream drain: launch a low-priority thread that calls cudaDeviceSynchronize() every 5–10 minutes during steady traffic windows to allow allocator to coalesce deferred frees. Pros: reduces fragmentation growth. Cons: small latency spikes and potential throughput impact.
- Cap KV-cache memory per model and add LRU trimming to keep overall working set bounded.
- Switch to synchronous cudaMalloc path for long-request allocation codepaths (configurable flag) — use only when pool fragmentation crosses threshold.
- Prevent mixing too many allocation sizes on same stream: reuse per-request temporary pool (thread-local) to reduce allocation churn across streams.

Longer-term fixes to evaluate:
- Implement custom arena coalescing logic in host-side pool: track freed extents across streams and opportunistically remap/merge when safe (requires careful stream-safety checks).
- Adopt a hybrid allocator: small allocations handled by a per-thread/free-list slab, and large workspace allocations reserved from a separate contiguous pool to guarantee large contiguous allocations.
- Work with NVIDIA to validate cudaMallocAsync deferred-free coalescing behavior under heavy multi-stream churn; file a vendor support ticket if needed.
- Improve KV-cache memory representation: prefer device-resident ring buffers or compressed cache entries to avoid creating many host pinned allocations.

Open questions & next steps:
- Can we reproduce with different CUDA versions (12.x) and driver combinations? We only tested 11.8/525.*; schedule matrix runs.
- Is there a measurable correlation between number of active streams and fragmentation rate? We need microbench that varies active streams explicitly.
- Is fragmentation worse on certain GPU architectures (A100 vs A10)? Run cross-arch reproducers.

Action items (owners):
- (Priya) Add background stream-drain feature branch and test perf impact on canary hosts. (ETA: 2024-11-09)
- (Liam) Create small microbench that alternates small ephemeral allocs on many streams + occasional large alloc to measure fragmentation growth per minute. (ETA: 2024-11-05)
- (Evelyn) Run matrix vs CUDA 12 / driver 550 on staging machines and report differences. (ETA: 2024-11-08)
- (Eng-SRE) Apply KV-cache soft-cap on a subset of Dedicated hosts for 48h to gauge failure rate change. (ETA: immediate)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider exposing "reserve_large_workspace" API: preallocate and pin a large contiguous buffer at startup to satisfy occasional big workspaces; can reduce memory noise but reduces available memory headroom. Good short stopgap for Dedicated customers who prioritize availability over peak utilization.
- Logging: extend allocator hooks to emit largest-contiguous-free every 5m and deferred_free_count. Hook into Console for early alerting.

Appendix: quick commands used
- nvtop / nvidia-smi dmon -s u
- python repro/run_workload.py --seq-dist mixed --concurrency 12 --kvcache 0.7
- Exported allocator hooks: export ALLOC_LOG=/tmp/alloc.log && tail -f /tmp/alloc.log

If you have other experiments or ideas, drop them here. Priority is to get a low-impact mitigation into canary and run matrix tests across CUDA/driver so we can attribute root cause (allocator semantics vs workload pattern) with confidence.
